correctness.rationale: Plancherel and 2-fold downsampling supply the exact normalized \(2\times2\) Fourier fiber. Its trace and determinant are directly computed from normalized heat multipliers; elementary polynomial signs prove that both singular-value squares strictly increase with alias-separation u, yielding sharp endpoint frame bounds. At zero spectral notch any finite family of time snapshots develops coinciding matrix columns at the alias collision; one snapshot never resolves both bands. For small gaps, direct Taylor expansion plus uniform \(t^2e^{-t}\) domination establishes convergence of maxima and of every maximizing time to the unique critical point \(t_0=1+e^{-2t_0}\). CHECK.py independently checks finite alias matrices, periodic Fourier observation Gram operators, and the optimization asymptotic; it is corroboration not continuum proof.

value.rationale: A stable two-snapshot design for the natural half-rate heat observation problem requires removal of a spectral neighborhood around the inevitable folding collision. The exact sharp reconstruction bounds and universal maximin observation lag show precisely how the best possible noise stability vanishes quadratically as that notch is closed; neither the known general invertibility criterion nor coarse blind-spot estimates quantify this. The minimal two-time acquisition and impossibility at any finite horizon without a notch provide an exact information-stability boundary. The result is specific but a complete, non-arbitrary parameter classification and an optimal design law.
